Working entry (`chk-hxm4imwn`, Epoch 4 — Inside the canvas, its last markerless entry): «Canvas keyboard path —
Circle Drawer's circles reached and acted on by keyboard; engine, snapshot and tree focus agree; Tab order in the shared
table (v040-11)», with three CARRYs folded below. Its wrap closes Epoch 4 and runs the leaf pass whole.

- Circle Drawer's circles are reached by keyboard: the canvas `circle-canvas` takes focus in the Tab walk, and keys move
  a current circle among its virtual nodes; the current circle is acted on by keyboard (selected, and its diameter
  dialog reachable as the double click reaches it today). [inferred] Today the canvas carries no `tabindex` and no key
  handler (`examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/circle_drawer.rs:310-350` reads `onclick` and `ondoubleclick` alone), so the
  canvas is no Tab stop and no circle is reachable by keyboard.

- Engine, snapshot and tree focus agree on the current circle: the engine's focus on the canvas element, the
  accessibility tree's `focus` and the snapshot's `focused` each read one consistent target — the stand's shared reader
  `focused` (`tests/blitz-tests/tests/common/mod.rs`) already asserts the snapshot's and the tree's focus agree.
  [inferred] A virtual node has no `NodeId`, so the engine's `focus_node_id` cannot hold it; how the tree's focus and the
  snapshot's `focused` name a virtual node while the engine holds the canvas is open at P3/P4 — the engine reads no
  `aria-activedescendant` (`accessibility_active_descendant_unread`, a stated limit on the founder's F2 of 2026-10-14
  and F3 B of 2026-10-18), and the declaration has no focus field (`custom_widget.rs:178`).

- Circle Drawer's Tab order enters the shared table: the stand's focus sequences live in
  `tests/blitz-tests/tests/common/mod.rs` (`tab_order`, `ENABLED_TAB_ORDER`, `LOAD_TAB_ORDER`, `ORDER_TAB_ORDER`,
  `CELLS_TAB_ORDER`), Circle Drawer's in none of them; the stand's keyboard walk (`stand_keyboard`) reads it beside the
  others.

- [founder's word, F1 «B1: выделение полем», not a fork — CARRY `cry-yr2aexmx`] A click inside a circle selects it and
  adds none: `VirtualNodeDeclaration` gains `selected`, written on the circle's accessibility node and read as the
  snapshot's existing `selected`, so a driver `click` on a circle's node settles with a diff naming that node
  (`differs: [selected]`), v040-11's «a click on one acts on its circle and its diff names it». A click on the canvas
  outside every circle still adds one. [inferred] The 7GUIs selection repaints the chosen circle filled (the prior
  forks file's F1 B1 row), which moves the committed canvas pins.

- v040-11's remaining stand readings on Circle Drawer: a circle refused `covered`, `off-screen` and `disabled`
  where the stand can make one so (the cap's notes: «also owed there: the stand's `covered`, `off-screen` and
  `disabled` readings»), keyboard reach being its last clause. [inferred] With these and the click clause, v040-11's
  acceptance reads whole on the stand and is claimable by this chunk; its binary reading waits on Circle Drawer being
  served («Cold-agent live run», CARRY `cry-owlk5tza`), which the acceptance does not name.
- Circle Drawer stays served by no `escher-session` role (the founder's «A: не сейчас», test-plan `amd-nasxjktn`).
- The lint reading virtual nodes (the founder's F6 B) is «Node-graph stand app»'s (`cry-ohadx5qs`) — not built here.
- A rotated or scaled canvas's virtual nodes are «Pan and zoom»'s.
- The engine's `aria-activedescendant` gap stays its stated limit unless P4 forks on it.

His answer: «B: номер узла»

The forks file's option **F2 B**: the covering node's index stays; no key and no id enters the canvas answer, the

The forks file's option **F6 B**: `off-screen`, `clipped` and `zero-size` on virtual nodes, `overlap` skipped on either

## Not put to him
F7 A (Circle Drawer stays unserved, his earlier «A: не сейчас») and F5 B (the coverage line, on his recorded F13 A).

# «Canvas keyboard path» — the answers to its forks, 2026-11-26

Answered by the escher overseer on 2026-11-26T06:58Z. The forks are the builder's `evidence/founder-forks.md` of the
chunk `2026-11-26-canvas-keyboard-path`. F1 B1 of the previous chunk («B1: выделение полем») is the founder's own and
stands beside every answer. No option that is the founder's is taken here.

## The answers — the operator's, a delegate's word
A row that rests only on one of these lands PROVISIONAL.

- **F1 A** — one Tab stop, as the CRUD list and Cells' grid: `circle-canvas` takes `tabindex` and the app's own key
  handler; the current circle is the selected one; the engine, the tree and the snapshot agree on `circle-canvas` at
  every step. B and C are not taken. State the limit an assistive technology meets (the current circle is read from
  `selected` alone) beside the CRUD list's, as a residual with its incubator line.
- **F2 A** — the four arrows move the selection in declared order, clamped; Enter opens the diameter dialog on the
  selected circle. No Home, End or Escape.
- **F2's side question: B** — a click on a circle focuses the canvas, so a `click` followed by a `press` acts on the
  circle the click selected. An agent that clicks a circle and presses Enter must not meet a key that goes nowhere.
  State what the focus events are and check them; if the buffered render makes the focus land a settle later, measure
  it and say so in the plan rather than hide it behind an extra `advance`.
- **F3 B** — a later-declared taken node of the same canvas whose region holds the target's centre covers it: a click
  on a circle under another is refused `covered`, never answered by selecting a different circle than the one named.
  The cause's name, remedy and order are unmoved; the four `covered` rows take one clause. State as a limit that a
  region is a bounding square, so a corner of a later square covers where its disc does not. The previous chunk's
  witness `a_circle_under_another_is_not_refused_covered` is restated to the new reading, with its red control. C is
  not taken (a layout made to serve a check).
- **F4 B** — while the diameter dialog is open every circle but the one it adjusts is declared disabled, read from an
  attribute of its own; `data-circles` keeps its form `x,y,d,id`. A click on a disabled circle is refused `disabled`.
- **F5 B** — `off-screen` is read on the stand after the page is scrolled with the dialog open, IF research measures
  it: the scroll offset and the circle's position are measured by a run before the plan pins them. If the page does
  not scroll far enough to put a circle's centre out of view, do not build a layout to force it: stop and tell me
  with the numbers.
- **The stand's circles under B1.** A second driver click at the canvas's centre now selects and adds none, so the
  stand's checks that stacked circles there are re-read; say in the plan how the stand gets separated circles (the
  fixture's `data-circles` writes, or clicks on declared offsets if a verb allows one — no new verb).

## Claims
v040-11 is claimed if every clause of its acceptance is read on the stand as written — keyboard reach, the click
naming its circle, `covered`, `off-screen`, `disabled` and `removed`, handler coverage. If F5 B cannot be measured, it
is not claimed and the stop above applies. No clause is narrowed here.

## Standing for the plan
The two Windows warnings (`stand_act_error_text.rs:27`, `seven_guis/tests/host_binary.rs:10`) are fixed and witnessed
by the CI windows job-log read with its unread-log guard. No key stands twice on a canvas line. No plan step deletes a
worktree or a build directory. A control enters with its red reading and a guard some input can turn red. A lock move
is not expected; if research meets one, stop.

current circle from `selected` alone, as it does on the CRUD list (a11y-plan · decision/active-descendant-unread).

A click inside a circle selects it and adds none (the founder's B1). `VirtualNodeDeclaration` gains `selected`, which is
written on the circle's accessibility node and read as the snapshot's existing `selected`. A driver `click` on a circle's
node therefore settles with a diff naming that node, `differs` holding `selected`. A click also focuses the canvas
(side question B). The probe measured the focus landing inside the click's own settled step in both layout modes
(evidence `probe-focus.md`), so a `click` followed by a `press` acts on the circle the click selected.
The stand also reads, on Circle Drawer:
- `covered`: a later-declared circle whose region holds the target's centre covers it (F3 B);
- `disabled`: while the dialog is open, every circle but the one it adjusts (F4 B);
- `removed`: `stale`, as the previous chunk proved.

`off-screen` is not read on the stand. The page with the dialog open moves 39 px at most, and no circle's centre leaves
the view (evidence `probe-offscreen.md`). v040-11 therefore stays pooled, its `off-screen` clause handed to an owner on
the P5 card. The canvas keeps its stated 700 × 400 when the dialog opens (`flex-shrink: 0`), the app defect the

(security-plan · decision/closed-value-field-no-widening).

1. **The declaration gains `selected`** (`packages/blitz-dom/src/node/custom_widget.rs`, `VirtualNodeDeclaration`):
   - add a public field `selected: Option<bool>` with a `///` doc: `None` states nothing; `Some(b)` is written as the
     node's selected state and read as the snapshot's `selected`. This keeps the node key's «written only where the
     element states it» (architecture · contract/node-keys/selected);
   - extend the struct's `///` summary line to name it;
   - give the other 3 literals `selected: None`: `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/virtual_node.rs:210`,
     `tests/blitz-tests/tests/fixtures/mod.rs:293`, `tests/blitz-tests/tests/virtual_nodes_declared.rs:41`. Circle
     Drawer's literal is step 4's.

5. **`covered` by a later circle** (F3 B) (`packages/escher-driver/src/execute.rs`, `covered` and the virtual-node
   target it reads):
   - for a target that is a virtual node, `covered` also reads true where a taken node its canvas declares LATER than
     the target has a region holding the target's region centre. The declarations are read through
     `DioxusDocument::virtual_nodes` on the target's canvas, in declaration order;
   - the element-hit reading stands before it, unchanged;
   - `check_target` and `Session::actions` share the one function, so the listed cause and the refusal stay one
     (security-plan · decision/actions-read-shares-target-check);
   - the fixed meaning of `covered` (`packages/escher-driver/src/refusal.rs:84-85`) replaces «a node a canvas declares
     reads covered only by an element over its region's centre, never by another node of its canvas» with «a node a
     canvas declares reads covered by an element over its region's centre, or by a node its canvas declares later
     whose region holds that centre — a region is the bounding box its canvas declares, so a later corner covers where
     the shape it paints does not»;
   - the cause's name, remedy and place in the order are unchanged (test-plan history `amd-4g5qmthy`), and the pinned
     copy of the text in `refusal.rs`'s tests (:271-272) takes the same words.

     inside the `#[cfg(unix)]` test at :18-36 (`grep -n "Command::\|Stdio" host_binary.rs`: lines 10, 29, 34-36).

      click-selects line, and the off-screen reading not taken on the stand. Its a11y-leg file count and
      stand-repeat named-target count are unmoved, no file being added to either.

    The sweep's record goes under research.md's `## Sweeps` at implement, a line a pattern
    (`circle-canvas`, `covered only by`, `Circle Drawer`).

11. **The controls**, one-shot `gate.py control` runs at implement, each entering with its red reading (tests S4):
    - **C1** (`circle_drawer.rs`): remove the disc-holds-the-point select arm, so every click adds. Case

- (a11y) Circle Drawer's canvas is one Tab stop: its walk reads `CIRCLE_DRAWER_TAB_ORDER` forward and back in both
  layout modes, with the engine's, the tree's and the snapshot's focus agreeing on `circle-canvas` at every step, and no
  circle the tree's focus (`cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked --test stand_keyboard --test stand_accessibility_ids`;
  a11y-plan · decision/stated-tab-order-walked; a11y-plan · decision/stand-shared-tab-order-table).

- (a11y) The arrows move the selection among the circles in declared order, clamped, the first arrow with none selected
  selecting the first. Enter opens the dialog on the selected circle, and a press with the dialog open changes nothing
  (`cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked --test stand_circle_nodes`, `the_keys_move_the_selection_in_declared_order`,
  `a_click_focuses_the_canvas_and_a_press_acts_on_its_circle`).

- (driver) A driver `click` on a circle's node selects it and adds none. The step settles, and its diff changes that
  node with `differs` holding `selected`, `data-circles` unchanged
  (`a_click_on_a_circle_node_selects_it_and_adds_none`; the founder's B1, inputs#I2).

- (driver) A click focuses the canvas within its own settled step. A `press enter` after it opens the dialog on the
  clicked circle. The focus change fires `blur` and `focusout` on the node that held focus, then `focus` and `focusin`
  on `circle-canvas`, in one settled step (`a_click_focuses_the_canvas_and_a_press_acts_on_its_circle`,
  `the_focus_events_of_a_canvas_click`; architecture · contract/event-dispatch/focus-change).

- (driver) A circle whose region centre a later-declared circle's region holds is refused `covered`, with nothing
  changed, and `actions` lists the same cause. A later square's corner covers where its disc does not, the stated limit
  (`a_circle_under_a_later_one_is_refused_covered`, `a_later_square_s_corner_covers_where_its_disc_does_not`; the
  `covered` meaning's name, remedy and order unchanged, `cargo test -p escher-driver --locked --lib`).

- (driver) With the dialog open, every circle but the one it adjusts reads not enabled and is refused `disabled` before
  `covered`; after Close every circle reads enabled (`an_open_dialog_disables_every_other_circle`).

- (dom) A declared `selected` of `Some(true)`, `Some(false)` and `None` reads `selected`, `unselected` and no word in the
  tree, the snapshot and its text, and a flip reads in a settled diff as `differs` holding `selected`
  (`cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked --test virtual_nodes_as_elements --test virtual_nodes_in_every_read --test virtual_nodes_declared`;
  security-plan · decision/closed-value-field-no-widening).

  (`stand_circle_nodes` reads the canvas bounds with the dialog open).

record.title: Virtual nodes inside a canvas
record.requirement: An app declares nodes inside a canvas with an author key, role, name and region, and the driver treats them as elements across the snapshot, diff, click, refusals, UI graph, actions, coverage, layout and exploration; Circle Drawer's circles are virtual nodes
record.observed_gap: A snapshot node needs an author id and a DOM element, so an agent sees a canvas as one opaque element; the UI graph reserves no id form for a non-DOM node; the layout verb reserves an app-canvas placing and the widget trait a commented accessibility tree.

verification.acceptance: On the stand, each Circle Drawer circle reads as a node with its key, role, name and region in the accessibility tree and the snapshot; a click on one acts on its circle and its diff names it; a covered, off-screen, disabled or removed one is refused with that cause; the UI graph, actions, handler coverage, layout explanation and exploration each list it; the circles are reached and acted on by keyboard.

record.notes:
2026-11-25 (2026-11-25-virtual-nodes-declared, wrap P7.3, on the operator's wrap directive point 6): not claimed, its first part proven. A canvas widget declares virtual nodes through the defaulted `Widget::virtual_nodes` (blitz-dom, behind `custom-widget`, additive, nothing sent upstream; overseer1's F2 A, delegate, PROVISIONAL), each a key, AccessKit's `Role` (F4 A), a name and a content-box region. `DioxusDocument::virtual_nodes` reads one canvas's declarations in process, in declaration order: a refused declaration reads its index and one closed reason, `EmptyKey` · `KeyHoldsSlash` · `DuplicateKey` (the first of a key kept) · `EmptyName` · `RegionOutside` (F5 A); each taken node reads the reserved id `{owner}///{key}`; a canvas before its first layout reads `NotLaidOut` and a stale or non-canvas node `NoCanvas`, with no panic. Proven by nine unit cases and `virtual_nodes_declared` in both layout modes (a region fitting the border box but not the content box refused), each refusal arm and the frame held red by controls K1–K14, green on linux, windows and macOS in CI#45538903978 at `a8ee63f0d`. Nothing crosses: `snapshot` and `graph` hold no `///` and no declared name (F3 A defers the names' crossing, the founder's fork), and a declaration change marks nothing and signals nothing (F1 B′, F6 A). Still owed to this capability: virtual nodes as elements in the accessibility tree, snapshot and diff, taking `click` and refused like elements («Virtual nodes as elements»), in every read («Virtual nodes in every read»), on Circle Drawer («Circle Drawer's circles as virtual nodes») and by keyboard («Canvas keyboard path»); the cap stays pooled.

2026-11-25 (2026-11-25-virtual-nodes-as-elements, phase P5): not claimed — not provable by this chunk. This chunk proves, on a fixture canvas a test declares and in both layout modes: the canvas's virtual nodes in the accessibility tree (children of its node, their ids, roles, names and declared disabled state) and from it in the snapshot and diff; `click` on one, settled, its diff naming the node it changed; its refusals `disabled`, `off-screen`, `covered`, `not-found` and `stale`; the id and name over MCP and in a kept check that replays (F3 A, the founder's word). The acceptance's stand surface (Circle Drawer's circles), the UI graph, actions, handler coverage, layout explanation and exploration listing a virtual node, and keyboard reach stay with «Circle Drawer's circles as virtual nodes», «Virtual nodes in every read» and «Canvas keyboard path».

element to the widget and returns before any default action (events/mod.rs:209-245), so Tab/Shift+Tab never move focus
off it. The plan's a11y acceptance (Tab walk forward and back) cannot read green without an engine change in a file

element and the widget still received the key — with its red control, name the file in research lists, flag it
upstreamable in the report.

title: evidence/founder-forks.md
body:
# Forks — 2026-11-26-canvas-keyboard-path (Canvas keyboard path)

Written at phase P4 on the operator's take-up direction (inputs#I1): every fork the plan meets other than F1 B1, which
the founder answered himself (inputs#I2, «B1: выделение полем») and which is not re-opened here. For each fork: what
crosses, the rule it meets, each option's measured cost, its dependences, whose it is and the most conservative option
that still builds the entry. Default: none — nothing below is taken until the operator relays the answers.

Run dir: `.andromeda/runs/2026-11-26T06-28-33-phase/` · scope `doc:2026-11-26-canvas-keyboard-path/scope` rev 3 ·
research rev 1 · HEAD `255a586fb`.

**Founder forks found: yes — F1 B and F1 C each change the tree's focus or active-descendant contract for every Dioxus
document behind `custom-widget`, and F1 C also reaches past his «Оставить записанным» on the active descendant.** F1 A
and every option of F2–F5 are the operator's. F1 A builds the entry with no founder word beyond B1.

**Standing beside every option: B1 itself** (the founder's word). `VirtualNodeDeclaration` gains `selected`:
`custom_widget.rs` +1 field and doc line; `dioxus_document.rs` +2 lines (`set_selected` beside `set_disabled`, :416);
`snapshot.rs` +1 line (the virtual branch reads `selected: tree_node.is_selected()`, :183); the 4 declaration literals
in 4 files take `selected: false` (re-derived: `git grep -n "VirtualNodeDeclaration {" -- packages tests examples`, 5
hits, 1 the definition; the prior forks file's 8 was at `a5d18f604`). The app: a selection signal with its declared
writes, a click inside a circle selecting it and adding none, the selected circle painted filled.

How costs were measured: file and line reads at HEAD `255a586fb`; name greps (each command named beside its count);
the rows files and histories of the run dir. No code-graph query ran (research is `derived-without-graph`). A cost
marked *derived* is read from source or CSS, not from a run.

Terms searched across all seven masters (`rec.py find --root . --doc all --text …`): `active descendant` (6 rows),
`tree's focus` (8), `accessibility-tree/focus` (2), `virtual node reads` (5), `keyboard-virtual-nodes` (1).

---

## F1 — How the engine, the tree and the snapshot name the current circle

**Today.** The tree's focus is `focus_node_id` filtered to the built nodes, else the window
(`accessibility.rs:105-110`). The virtual nodes are appended afterwards in dioxus-native-dom
(`dioxus_document.rs:400-420`), which never sets `tree.focus`. The snapshot reads `focused` as `id == tree.focus`
(`snapshot.rs:122`, `:183`). The stand's shared reader `focused` (`tests/blitz-tests/tests/common/mod.rs`) asserts that
the snapshot's focused ids equal the tree's focus. The canvas carries no `tabindex` and no key handler
(`circle_drawer.rs:310-352`).

**What crosses / the rule it meets.** Under every option the canvas becomes a Tab stop and its key handler is the app's
own: a focused canvas is outside the engine's Enter and Space arms (security-plan
`decision/enter-activates-focused-control`). Under B the adapter and the snapshot get a focus on a node with no element.
Under C they get an engine-written active descendant and a `highlighted` reading on a virtual node. Both are closed
values inside the ratified carriers (security-plan `decision/boundary-widening-rule`), but each changes a ratified
engine contract.

| Option | What it does | Measured / derived cost |
|---|---|---|
| A | One Tab stop, as the CRUD list and Cells' grid: `circle-canvas` takes `tabindex: "0"` and an app `onkeydown`; the current circle is the selected one (B1's `selected`); the engine, the tree and the snapshot all read focus on `circle-canvas` | App only (`circle_drawer.rs`, the `cells.rs:414-436` form); no engine or dioxus-native-dom line beyond B1. Rows: a11y `absence/keyboard-virtual-nodes` retired; a11y `decision/stated-tab-order-walked` gains Circle Drawer. An assistive technology learns the current circle from `selected` alone — the CRUD list's stated limit (a11y `decision/active-descendant-unread`) |
| B | The tree's focus names the selected circle's virtual node while the engine holds the canvas; the snapshot follows the tree | `dioxus_document.rs` *derived* ~6–10 lines (after the loop at :400-420, `tree.focus` set to the selected node's tree id where `focus_node_id` is the canvas); `snapshot.rs` none; the shared `focused` reader and `stand_keyboard`'s three-way agreement re-stated, because the engine's focus is then the canvas while the tree's is the circle. Rows amended: architecture and a11y-plan `contract/accessibility-tree/focus`, security-plan `decision/accessibility-focus-built-nodes-only`, architecture `contract/snapshot/virtual-node` (focused), a11y-plan `decision/stated-tab-order-walked` (what «agree» means), architecture `decision/hit-focus-form-engine-changes` (its tally) |
| C | The canvas names the selected circle as its active descendant, engine-written as the open select list's is (`accessibility.rs:232-240`); the tree's focus stays on the canvas; the snapshot reads that circle `highlighted` | `dioxus_document.rs` *derived* ~3–5 lines (`set_active_descendant` on the canvas node); `snapshot.rs`, the `highlighted` set taking virtual ids. Rows amended: architecture `contract/accessibility-tree/active-descendant` and `contract/node-keys/highlighted` (an open select's row alone today), a11y-plan `contract/snapshot/open-list-highlighted-row`, design-system `contract/select-accessibility/open-select`. It reaches past a11y-plan `decision/active-descendant-unread` and `decision/active-descendant-kept-unread` (the founder's F2 «Оставить записанным», 2026-10-14, F3 B 2026-10-18), though no page `aria-activedescendant` is read |

**Dependences.** F2 (the keys that move the selection). B1 is the current-circle state under every option. Under B a
selection change must also mark the changed set, or a windowed adapter never hears the focus move (architecture
`decision/declaration-change-marks-nothing` would be amended).

**Whose.** A — the operator's (an app change; the security history: «the Circle Drawer canvas taking a Tab stop and a
key handler that moves a current circle follows the same app-level shape», the Cells precedent ratified on the founder's
F13). B — the founder's: «Making a virtual node the tree's focus is an engine change for every document behind the
feature, so it goes to the founder» (security-plan history, 2026-10-31-engine-debts). C — the founder's: it reaches
past his recorded word on the active descendant.

**Most conservative that builds the entry:** A. The entry asks that the engine, the snapshot and the tree agree, and
under A they agree on `circle-canvas` at every step.

---

## F2 — The keys on the focused canvas, and what acts on the current circle

**Today.** The diameter dialog opens only by a double click on the nearest circle (`circle_drawer.rs:339-358`). The
driver's `press` takes 12 key names (`schema.rs:22-35`: tab, enter, escape, backspace, delete, space, the four arrows,
home, end) and acts on what holds focus (`execute.rs:292`).

**What crosses / the rule it meets.** Nothing new: `press` keys are already call content in a kept check (security-plan
`decision/kept-check-call-content`). Under F1 A the app's key handler must be the actor (security-plan history
2026-10-13).

| Option | Keys | Measured / derived cost |
|---|---|---|
| A | The four arrows move the selection to the previous or next circle in declared order, clamped, the first arrow with none selected selecting the first; Enter opens the diameter dialog on the selected circle | App only; `stand_keyboard` rows for Circle Drawer; the canvas `onkeydown` joins the UI graph's handlers and the coverage tables (`HANDLERS_AT_BOOT`, `UNEXERCISED_AFTER_DRIVES`); per the Cells history (amd-dbogce46) a key handler may move `stand_non_lean_tasks`' counts |
| B | A, plus Home and End to the first and last circle, and Escape clearing the selection | as A, +3 match arms and their rows |

**Dependences.** F1 (under B or C the same keys also move the tree's focus or active descendant). B1: a selection
change repaints a fill, so each move changes the canvas answer's lines.

**Whose.** The operator's (app behaviour, no crossing).

**Most conservative that builds the entry:** A.

**A side question in the same class: does a pointer click on a circle focus the canvas?** Today it does not: a click
on a custom-widget target runs no click walk and clears no focus (architecture `decision/widget-click-synthesis`). A —
unchanged (a mouse user then Tabs to the canvas before the keys act). B — the app's `onclick` calls `set_focus` through
its `MountedData` handle (the buffered render, architecture `decision/dioxus-bridge-buffered-render`), so the keys act
after a click, the focus events firing. The operator's; most conservative: A.

---

## F3 — `covered` on the stand (the prior chunk's F4, open as CARRY `cry-yr2aexmx` states)

**Today.** A virtual node reads `covered` only by an element over its region's centre (F12 A, delegate, PROVISIONAL:
architecture and security-plan `contract/refusal-causes/covered`, a11y-plan `contract/driver-click-refusals/covered`,
test-plan `contract/refusal-cause/covered`). The stand has no such element: the dialog `.cd-dialog` lies in flow below
the canvas (`circle_drawer.rs:447-458`, `margin-top: 16px`), never over it. `stand_circle_nodes.rs:348`
`a_circle_under_another_is_not_refused_covered` pins it.

**What crosses / the rule it meets.** Nothing new crosses (a closed cause word). The meaning text of `covered` is one of
the eight fixed texts (ratified 2026-10-18); a clause was added to it once with its name, remedy and order unmoved
(test-plan `amd-4g5qmthy`).

| Option | What it does | Measured / derived cost |
|---|---|---|
| A | Kept: elements alone cover. Under B1 a click on a circle under another selects the top one, so the diff names the top circle, not the one named | 0 code; the stand witness re-read under B1 (the diff names `c2`); v040-11's «covered … refused with that cause» is not read on the stand |
| B | A later-declared taken node of the same canvas whose region holds the target's centre covers it | `execute.rs` `covered` (one function, shared with `actions` through `check_target`); the four covered rows above take one clause; measured by the prior forks file on its fixture sequence: 2 of 12 circles and 26 of 100 read `covered`; on the stand every centre click stacks at (348,198), so all but the last of N circles read `covered` |
| C | The app draws its dialog over the canvas (absolute position), so the dialog's element covers the circles under it | `circle_drawer.rs` CSS; the dialog's layout pins move (`stand_lint`, `stand_contrast` if it reads the dialog, the snapshot bounds); no rule changes |

**Dependences.** B1 (without B, a click on a covered circle selects the top one). F4 and F5: v040-11's claim needs all
three stand readings.

**Whose.** The operator's (the rows B changes are a delegate's PROVISIONAL; the cause's name, remedy and order are
unmoved). C — the operator's (an app layout change).

**Most conservative that builds the entry:** A (the entry does not name `covered`).

---

## F4 — `disabled` on the stand

**Today.** Every circle is declared `disabled: false` (`circle_drawer.rs:230`). A virtual node reads `enabled` from its
declaration (architecture `contract/snapshot/virtual-node`, a11y-plan `contract/snapshot/enabled`).

| Option | What it does | Measured / derived cost |
|---|---|---|
| A | None: no circle is ever disabled on the stand | 0 code; v040-11's «disabled … refused» is read on fixtures alone |
| B | While the diameter dialog is open, every circle but the one it adjusts is declared disabled | App: the widget reads one more attribute (for example `data-adjusting`, leaving the founder-ratified `data-circles` form `x,y,d,id` of layout-templates `decision/circle-drawer-circles-painted-on-canvas` unmoved); a stand check; the snapshot's `enabled` on circles moves while the dialog is open |

**Whose.** The operator's (app behaviour; `disabled` is a closed reading in a ratified carrier).

**Most conservative that builds the entry:** A.

---

## F5 — `off-screen` on the stand

**Today.** *Derived from CSS, not measured by a run:* the canvas border box is 704 × 404 under the toolbar
(`circle_drawer.rs:427-440`), inside the 800 × 600 viewport (architecture `decision/stand-pinned-environment`), and every
region is cut to the 696 × 396 content box (`circle_drawer.rs:83-95`), so every circle lies in view while the page
stands unscrolled.

| Option | What it does | Measured / derived cost |
|---|---|---|
| A | None: no circle is off-screen on the stand | 0 code; v040-11's «off-screen … refused» is read on fixtures alone |
| B | With the dialog open the page grows past 600 px (*derived*: the dialog is in flow below the canvas); a `scroll` of `circle-close` into view moves the viewport, and a circle near the canvas's top edge then lies above it | A stand check; the scroll offset and the circle's position need measuring first; a circle off-screen only after a scroll the stand chose |

**Whose.** The operator's.

**Most conservative that builds the entry:** A.

---

## The capability this entry was to close

v040-11's acceptance reads «On the stand, … a covered, off-screen, disabled or removed one is refused with that cause»
beside «the circles are reached and acted on by keyboard». Under the most conservative set (F1 A · F2 A · F3 A · F4 A ·
F5 A) only `removed` (`stale`, proven by the prior chunk) is read on the stand. v040-11 then stays pooled, and this entry
is Epoch 4's last: no later markerless entry names it. Each of F3 B or C, F4 B and F5 B adds one stand reading. The
other ways to close it — re-scoping the acceptance to «on fixtures» for those three causes (a narrowing, so the
founder's), or carrying it to a later entry — are a `## Beyond the plan` row, not a choice made here.

## Not a fork — what the intent already decides, reaching the founder at the wrap

- B1 makes `selected` cross on a virtual node: a closed bool in the ratified snapshot, diff and adapter carriers
  (security-plan `decision/closed-value-field-no-widening`) — no widening; the rows that say a virtual node reads no
  `selected` (architecture `contract/snapshot/virtual-node`, `contract/nodes-widgets/virtual-nodes`) are re-stated on
  his word, already given.
- This entry's wrap closes Epoch 4: by the playbook's `rul-3ndrhilc` (Provisional discharge) it lists every standing
  PROVISIONAL mark for the founder's batch word. Among them are the delegate rows F3 B would amend.

## The most conservative set that still builds the entry

F1 A · F2 A · F3 A · F4 A · F5 A, with the side question's A. It builds the canvas as one Tab stop whose arrows select a
circle and whose Enter opens its dialog, the engine, the tree and the snapshot agreeing on `circle-canvas`. It builds
B1's click selection, Circle Drawer's Tab order in the shared table, and both windows warnings fixed. v040-11 stays
pooled with no owner (the row above). No founder word is needed beyond B1.

# Side question B probe — does a click's `set_focus` land in the click's own settled step?

Run at P4 on the operator's side-question answer (inputs#I4), at HEAD `255a586fb`, in the detached probe worktree
`escher-probe-ckp` (left in place), sharing the repository's build directory:
`cargo test --locked -p blitz-tests --test probe_focus -- --nocapture`, a probe file never committed.

The probe made two changes to `circle_drawer.rs`, neither committed:
- `tabindex: "0"` on `circle-canvas`;
- at the end of its async `onclick`, `drop(handle.set_focus(true))` on the canvas's `MountedData`, the form
  `cells.rs:517` uses.

The first probe's `flex-shrink: 0` stayed in the worktree; it does not bear on focus.

## Measured (both layout modes, the same readings)

| Step | Driver step | Snapshot focused | Engine focus (element id) |
|---|---|---|---|
| boot | — | none | `/html:0` (the root element; `contract/harness-inspect/focused`) |
| `click circle-canvas` | settled true; diff changed `circle-undo`, `circle-canvas` | `circle-canvas` | `circle-canvas` |
| `advance 1` | — | `circle-canvas` | `circle-canvas` |

## Reading

The focus lands inside the click's own settled step: the step's diff names `circle-canvas` changed, and the snapshot
and the engine agree on it. No later settle and no `advance` are needed (the buffered render,
architecture `decision/dioxus-bridge-buffered-render`). The probe read neither the focus events nor the tree's focus
apart from the snapshot, which reads the tree's focus (`snapshot.rs:122`). The plan's check asserts both.

# F5 B probe — does Circle Drawer's page scroll with the diameter dialog open?

Run at P4 on the operator's F5 B («IF research measures it», inputs#I4), at HEAD `255a586fb`, in a detached probe
worktree beside the repository (`escher-probe-ckp`, left in place), sharing the repository's build directory:
`cargo test --locked -p blitz-tests --test probe_offscreen -- --nocapture`, a probe file never committed. Both layout
modes read identically. The canvas is booted through `session_common::circle_drawer`. The dialog is opened by two
driver clicks on `circle-canvas` with no `advance` between them, which the virtual clock reads as a double click. The
viewport is the stand's pinned 800 × 600.

## Measured (both layout modes, the same numbers)

| Step | Viewport scroll | `circle-canvas` bounds | `circle-close` bounds | Circles |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| boot | (0, 0) | x 50, y 106, 700 × 400 | absent | none |
| two centre clicks (dialog open) | (0, 0) | x 50, y 106, 700 × **324** | x 360.94, y 531, 78.14 × 32 | c1, c2 at x 380, y 286, 40 × 40 |
| `scroll circle-close` (accepted) | (0, 0) | unchanged | unchanged | unchanged |

## Reading

## 2026-11-26-canvas-keyboard-path — Input Validation: 1 row(s)
**Section:** Input Validation
**Change:** ~ contract/diff-node/selected · promise: was «A boolean, written only where the element states it.»; now «A boolean, written only where the element or a virtual node's declaration states it.»
**Why:** contract/diff-node/selected: A canvas's virtual node now states selected through its declaration and the diff writes it, so «written only where the element states it» is false; the cascade's old-wording sweep found it (cascade-patterns.toml sel-aria-only). — on relayed verbatim by the escher overseer, 2026-11-25, inputs#I2: the founder's F1 «B1: выделение полем»
**Ref:** .andromeda/runs/2026-11-26T09-56-13-wrap/

- **Keyboard harness:** a Tab and Shift+Tab key-press focus check exists on the stand, driven through the harness's `press` / `press_with` (`stand_snapshot_state.rs`); since 2026-10-13-range-input-interaction a range-input key and click check runs in both layout modes (`range_input_interaction.rs`: a 7-row keys table and a 5-row clicks table, one `input` per change and none on a no-change Home, the input focused after every click, a disabled range taking neither keys nor a click), and on the stand `stand_act_range.rs` moves the Timer slider through the driver by click and key, an arrow step after two Tabs leaving it focused with role `Slider`, its name and the forward focus sequence unchanged; since 2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness `stand_keyboard.rs` drives Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Space and the CRUD list's keys headlessly on the four lean tasks through the same `press` / `press_with`, reading the focused node back per step, in both layout modes, and pins the flight booker's `select#flight-type` (named `Flight type` by `aria-label`, its second Tab stop) moving its choice by its arrows (`the_flight_type_select_moves_its_choice_by_its_arrows`), and walks the load page's `LOAD_TAB_ORDER`, Cells' `CELLS_TAB_ORDER` and Circle Drawer's stated Tab order forward and back in both layout modes, the load page's button taking Enter and Space, Cells' arrows and Enter opening the moved-to cell's editor and its value committing by keyboard; a select key and typeahead check runs in both layout modes — `select_interaction` (a keys table and a typeahead table, one `input` and one `change` per change and none for no change, the typed text kept for one second of the document's clock, a disabled select taking no key and no click) and, through the driver, `stand_act_select` (Tab `fx-before` → `fx-pick` → `fx-named` → `fx-after` → `fx-before`, the disabled `fx-off` skipped, an option chosen by a click then a key) — both in the `a11y` leg, both three rounds in the `stand-repeat` leg, `stand_act_select` by its `stand_` prefix and `select_interaction` by the leg's named `--test` list; the select list's keyboard and focus coverage is headless — `select_popup`, `stand_act_popup` and `stand_keyboard`'s list walks (`the_flight_type_walk_holds_with_its_list_open_and_after_each_close`, `a_click_opens_the_list_focus_stays_on_the_select_and_the_walk_goes_on_from_it`) assert SC 2.1.1 and 2.4.3 on it in both layout modes, `stand_keyboard` in the `a11y` leg and the other two outside it, in the workspace `test` leg and three `stand-repeat` rounds, and the windowed list is read and not run.

- Stand markup (attributes only): the flight booker's date inputs state `aria-invalid`, and the stand states no `aria-pressed` — the flight booker's mode is one `select#flight-type`, whose options state its choice by `selected`; the CRUD list is a `listbox` and its rows `option`s with `aria-selected`. Since 2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness (the operator's decision) the list `crud-list` takes `tabindex="0"` and an `onkeydown` — the third CRUD Tab stop — and, focused, ArrowDown selects the next visible row (the first when none is selected), ArrowUp the previous, Home the first and End the last, as a row's click does. One gap stands open: the rows are not focusable and the tree's focus is the list, never the option — the builder reads no `aria-activedescendant`, so an assistive technology learns the current row only from its `selected` reading; an `aria-activedescendant` read in the builder, or a roving focus, is SC 4.1.2 work outside the tier-0 target, kept unread on the founder's F2 (2026-10-14) and pinned by `accessibility_active_descendant_unread` (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18). The second, the list's empty accessible name, closed at 2026-10-14-stand-a11y-assertions: the list is named `People` by `aria-label`. Cells: `cells-grid`, named `Cells` by `aria_label` with no role, is one Tab stop; the arrows move `current`, clamped, and bring the cell into view; Enter opens the editor on `current`, focused, and the editor's Enter commits and returns focus to the grid; Tab leaving an open editor commits it; `.cells-grid:focus .cell.current` draws a 2px outline in the stand accent; role and cell semantics stay out, owned by residual `res-wvatzhpe` (re-carried at 0.3.0, target: next). body: escher is a native-API engine library with no served network API in a default build, no default feature set serving a TCP or UDP port — two `blitz-net` tests alone binding TCP on loopback, served by no binary — and no authentication; the opt-in `devtools` feature, off in every default feature set, builds a CDP devtools server binding TCP on 127.0.0.1 at the port `BLITZ_CDP_PORT` names, with no Origin check and no authentication (a boundary widening by upstream merge, ratified); its one default listener is local — the driver session's owner-only Unix-domain socket, which carries the session's lifecycle and, since 2026-10-10-driver-cli, driver calls and their answers (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-10); since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface the same calls and answers also cross to an MCP client over the `escher-session mcp` role's own stdio, no listener (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-10). Its risk is in what it ingests: arbitrary remote HTML/CSS/images/fonts/sub-documents, JavaScript run by `blitz-vibey-script`, CLI arguments of the examples, and the local desktop's drag-and-drop, an untrusted input source to the engine and to a Dioxus app's handlers carrying strings and file paths chosen by the user's OS session. The application-level threat model is NOT YET MEASURED.

- **`file:` reads** → blitz-net reads a `file:` URL only for a `file:` document or a top-level load — any other stylesheet, `@import`, font, image or iframe load refused before a disk read with `FileForbidden` (fixed text, no URL or path), and the browser app names no `file:` favicon and drops a `file:` navigation silently for any other document, remote pages included — and where it reads, any path with no restriction — through `Url::to_file_path` off wasm, a non-path URL a typed `InvalidInput` error; the WPT net provider joins request paths onto the WPT base; the Dioxus native bridge's dropped-file reader reads a dropped file's metadata and bytes through std::fs with no path restriction (upstream's design, ratified).
